History:
- Chief complaint: Acute headache starting this morning on the left side; woke at ~5:30 am with a “really horrible” headachy sensation; headache persists.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began waking up this morning; currently ongoing; initially painful when lying down but gradually eases with time; pain is now present at rest.
- Character/associated features: Unilateral left-sided pain; sensitivity to bright lights (photophobia) noted; no neck stiffness; no fever; no significant nausea; brief dizziness on waking which resolved.
- Triggers/stress: Ongoing work-related stress for about two months; sleep/work backlog; history of anxiety; previously weighted toward tension-type headaches but this episode is more unilateral.
- Prior episodes: Has a history of headaches but none as severe as this; previous headaches tended to be more frontal and bilateral.
- Family history: No migraines in family; mother has anxiety.
- Medications: Sertraline (for anxiety) ongoing; took Paracetamol this morning with little relief (dose not documented).
- Social history: Lives with partner; non-smoker; has a cat; exercises ~3 times per week (running); diet described as OK; stress high; no other illnesses reported.
- Safety: No thoughts of self-harm; patient reassuring.

Past Medical History:
- Anxiety disorder; on Sertraline (dose not documented).
- No known hypertension; blood pressure has not been checked (no documentation of BP measurements).
- Allergies: None documented.
- Medications: Sertraline; Paracetamol (taken this morning) (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Physical Examination:
- Neck stiffness: No
- Fever: No
- Photophobia: Mild sensitivity to bright lights
- Nausea: Not present
- Dizziness: Brief at onset, resolved
- Exam not performed directly; patient reports symptoms as above.
- No other physical findings documented.

Impression:
- Headache syndrome with unilateral left-sided onset and photophobia; differential includes migraine-type headache and tension-type headache in the context of stress/anxiety.  

Management Plan:
- Medications:
  - Ibuprofen (first-line for migraine-type headache) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Paracetamol (continued; dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Non-pharmacologic:
  - Consider reducing work-related stress; advise taking time off work (self-certify for one week).
  - Counseling options via a local service; link to be provided for self-referral.
  - Sleep target: at least 7–8 hours per night.
  - Hydration: 1.5–2 liters of fluids per day (excluding coffee/tea).
- Follow-up:
  - Recheck in one week.
  - If symptoms persist or worsen, consider blood tests or alternate diagnoses; otherwise continue current plan.
  - Patient advised to contact clinic sooner if red flags or sudden worsening.
- Education/Resources:
  - Summary note and link to danger signs of headaches will be provided.
  - Self-monitoring and re-evaluation plan discussed.

Patient Summary:
- The patient presented with an acute left-sided headache since this morning, with photophobia and mild dizziness but no fever or neck stiffness. Differential includes migraine-type headache and tension-type headache related to stress/anxiety. Initiated ibuprofen and paracetamol as needed, with plans to reduce work stress, pursue counseling, ensure adequate sleep and hydration, and follow up in one week. If not improved, further testing may be considered.

Key Takeaways:
- Start ibuprofen as first-line treatment for presumed migraine-type headache; continue paracetamol as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Address contributing factors: reduce work-related stress (consider time off), pursue counseling, ensure adequate sleep and hydration.
- Schedule follow-up in one week; seek earlier care if red flags or worsening symptoms.

Next Steps:
- Monitor response to NSAID therapy; reassess at follow-up in 1 week.
- If not improving, discuss potential blood tests and alternative workup.
- Provide and review danger-signs resource; facilitate self-referral for counseling; ensure adequate sleep and hydration.

Quality checks:

  - Vitals (blood pressure, pulse, temperature) not provided.
  - Full medication reconciliation with doses/routes/frequencies not documented (Sertraline and Paracetamol noted; doses not specified).
  - No formal mental status exam performed; mood assessment notes are limited to patient history.
- Internal conflicts:
  - None identified; differential clearly stated with two possible etiologies.
- Transcript quality:
  - Conversation is generally clear but contains informal language and some repetition; no major inaudible sections.
